sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: House Democrats Demand Trump Documents Be Retained
cards.content: House Democrats are demanding that the Interior Department retain documents related to President Donald Trump's construction projects around Washington after whistleblowers warned that key paperwork has already been destroyed before Democrats take power. The warnings come as the Trump administration is signaling it will accelerate plans for moving ahead with the projects, a key part of what the president sees as his legacy. The top Democrat in the House Natural Resources committee, Rep. Jared Huffman, plans to issue letters to the Interior Department and other federal agencies and private companies, requesting that they preserve all records and data responsive to oversight. Multiple credible whistleblowers have approached Huffman's committee in recent weeks to voice concern that the Interior Department is getting rid of records in anticipation of forthcoming scrutiny. The agency oversees much of the national parkland Trump wants to use for his projects.

cards.title: US Charges Iran-Backed Operatives Over Terror Plots in US and Europe
cards.content: The US Department of Justice (DOJ) has announced charges against three Iran-backed operatives for their alleged involvement in a string of plots in the US and Europe. The DOJ claims that the trio orchestrated a terrorist plot at an air force base in the UK, which led to the declaration of a major incident in September. The suspects allegedly planned attacks in Europe, including seven incidents in the UK, and were involved in nearly 20 attempted attacks in support of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and the Iran-backed Iraqi militia Kataib Hezbollah. The FBI Director has described the accused as determined to commit terrorist attacks in Europe and the US, and the suspects' actions allegedly included arranging logistics for the RAF Fairford terrorist plot and procuring materials to use in the attacks.

cards.title: California voters reject billion-dollar wealth tax
cards.content: California voters rejected Proposition 40, a one-time 5% wealth tax on residents with a net worth of over $1 billion. The measure's opponents, backed by billionaire funders and groups, spent tens of millions of dollars on ads against the proposition. Proponents argued the tax was necessary to address federal healthcare spending cuts and estimated it could raise $100 billion, enough to cover the shortfall for about five years. The battle over Proposition 40 was one of the most expensive political fights in the country, with Google co-founder Sergey Brin funneling $100 million to a group trying to defeat the tax. California's Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom and Gov.-elect Xavier Becerra opposed the measure, while progressive Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Ro Khanna supported it.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Scientists Control Atomic Nucleus Spin Using Radio Waves
cards.content: Scientists at Delft University of Technology have made a breakthrough in controlling the magnetic spin of a single atomic nucleus using radio waves. The experiment, published in Nature Communications, challenges their understanding of atomic magnetism by showing that nuclear spin can be manipulated under conditions where it was not expected to respond. Unlike electron spin, nuclear spin is extremely weak and better shielded from its surroundings. The researchers used a modified scanning tunneling microscope to direct electrical signals at individual atoms, achieving control by adapting double magnetic resonance to work with a single atom. This breakthrough could support new methods for storing and reading quantum information in the future, but practical applications remain uncertain. Further investigation is needed to understand the physical mechanism behind the observed behavior.

cards.title: SoftBank Reports $7 Billion Net Loss Amid AI Investments
cards.content: SoftBank, a Japanese investment giant, reported a net loss of $7 billion in its fiscal second quarter, mainly due to losses tied to AI data center equipment procurement and Intel share declines. The company also recorded a $3.7 billion loss in the six months ended September 30, largely due to changes in procurement plans for power generation equipment for AI data center projects in the US. SoftBank's Vision Fund segment swung to a loss, while its AI computing segment saw higher revenue. The company's Vision Funds segment recorded investment gains, and its cumulative investment in OpenAI stands at $54.6 billion, with a fair value of $99.6 billion. SoftBank shares closed 13.9% higher following the earnings release, with the company highlighting its AI infrastructure investments, including a 20-year lease agreement with OpenAI for eight gigawatts of IT capacity at a data center project in Ohio.

cards.title: New Broadway Musical 'Galileo' Brings Astronomer's Story to Life
cards.content: A new Broadway musical, 'Galileo,' brings the life of the pioneering astronomer Galileo Galilei to the stage. The show, which opens December 6 at the Shubert Theatre in New York City, features Raúl Esparza and Joy Woods, and tells the story of Galileo's defiance of the Roman Catholic Church's dogma, which led to his fall from favor and eventual house arrest. Director Michael Mayer and coproducer Neil deGrasse Tyson hope that the show's themes of standing up for what is objectively true against dogmatic forces will resonate with audiences in today's political climate. The musical draws heavily on real events, including Galileo's experiments and his confrontation with the Roman Inquisition, and features stunning effects designed by Ethan Tobman, the creative director for Taylor Swift's Eras Tour.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Alzheimer's Breakthrough: Specific Brain Cells Linked to Disease
cards.content: A massive genetic analysis of 2.8 million people has led to a breakthrough in understanding Alzheimer's disease, revealing specific brain cells that may influence the condition. The study, published in Nature, identified 127 regions of human DNA associated with Alzheimer's risk, including 48 previously unknown. Researchers found that microglia, immune cells in the brain, and specific types of nerve cells may play a key role in the disease's development. The findings provide new leads for investigating potential treatments and offer a more detailed view of the biological processes involved. The study's lead, Danielle Posthuma, emphasized the importance of connecting genetic risk factors to specific biological processes, which can help in identifying potential targets for treatment.

cards.title: ER Doctor Fails to Recognize Rare Condition, Baby Dies
cards.content: Stephanie and Eric Biesenbach took their 11-day-old daughter Gwen to the emergency room when she started bleeding from her belly button. Despite the ER doctor, Nicole Malouf, trying various methods to stop the bleeding, Gwen's condition continued to deteriorate. Malouf failed to recognize the signs of vitamin K deficiency bleeding, a rare but potentially life-threatening condition, and did not give Gwen the vitamin K shot. Gwen's bleeding worsened, and she eventually died. An investigation by the Texas Medical Board found that Malouf had failed to meet the standard of care in her treatment of Gwen and that her lack of timely care ultimately resulted in Gwen's death. Malouf was required to take 24 hours of continuing medical education and inform her employers of the disciplinary action taken against her.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: India Hit by Extreme Weather Events on 92% of Days in 2026, Resulting in 3,220 Deaths
cards.content: In the first nine months of 2026, India experienced extreme weather events on 92% of days, resulting in 3,220 deaths, damage to 4.25 million hectares of crops, and the destruction of 128,334 houses. Uttar Pradesh and Himachal Pradesh were the most affected, with Uttar Pradesh reporting the highest death toll. The report also found that nearly every part of India was affected, with over 16,000 deaths and 20.6 million hectares of crops damaged between 2022 and 2026.

cards.title: Human metabolism's carbon dioxide emissions rise 74% in 30 years
cards.content: A new study by the University of Bath has found that the amount of carbon dioxide produced by human metabolism has increased by 74% over the past three decades, with the global total reaching an estimated 2.05 billion metric tons annually by 2015. The study, published in The Lancet Planetary Health, analyzed thousands of real-world measurements of CO2 production in people of all ages and found that the increase is mainly due to population growth, with more than 60% of the rise attributed to an increase in the number of people rather than a significant change in the amount produced by each individual. The researchers suggest that accounting for this activity could help scientists more accurately predict how effective carbon reduction strategies may be.

cards.title: Srinagar's Water Crisis Worsens due to Climate Change
cards.content: In Srinagar, a water crisis has been ongoing for years, causing daily struggles for residents like Mehak and Zamrood. The absence of a regular water supply has led to the installation of tanks and a hand pump at their homes. Climate change is affecting Doodh Ganga, a vital source of drinking water, causing erratic water supply, low flow, and dry taps. The river's water availability is decreasing due to rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and declining snowmelt. The Kashmir Valley's 24 watersheds, including Doodh Ganga, are experiencing similar impacts.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Shadowbox Studios hosts major film and TV productions
cards.content: Shadowbox Studios in Shinfield, Wokingham, is a state-of-the-art complex with 18 sound stages, including two with over 40,000 square feet of floor space each. The studios have hosted major film and television productions such as Avengers: Doomsday, Ghostbusters: Frozen Empire, Squid Game: The Challenge, and Ebenezer, starring Johnny Depp and Rupert Grint. With its climate controls, soundproofing, and large stages, the complex can be transformed into different worlds for various productions, making it an attractive location for filmmakers. The UK's film and television industry is growing, with spending reaching £6.8 billion in 2025, and the country's variety of landscapes and historic locations also makes it an attractive location for shoots.

cards.title: Series Breaks Sales Records with Sixth Installment
cards.content: Sarah J Maas's blockbuster series, A Court of Thorns and Roses, has broken sales records with its sixth book, A Court of Splintered Harmony. The series, known for its brutal wars, faeries, and spicy sex scenes, has become a dominating force in fiction, particularly among women under 35. The success of Maas's series has been driven by BookTok, a section of TikTok dedicated to book commentary, and the author has sold over 100 million copies worldwide. The series is a blend of romance and fantasy, also known as romantasy, which has become a multi-million-dollar subgenre. According to Dr. Jodi McAlister, the series' appeal lies in its complex world-building, intricate plotlines, and the promise of a happy ending, providing a comforting escape for readers.

cards.title: ITV Wales cuts programs, reduces staff in cost-saving moves
cards.content: ITV Wales is planning to cut two long-running programs, Coast and Country and Backstage, as part of cost-cutting measures. The broadcaster aims to reduce the number of producer roles from six to two and make more programs in the studio rather than on location. These changes will not affect the news and current affairs programs, and ITV Wales is consulting with staff about the proposals. The move is part of efforts to ease cost pressure amid the industry's significant economic strain. ITV Wales is also restructuring its teams to work more flexibly, while protecting its commitments to the audience and regulator, Ofcom. In related news, Sky has agreed to buy ITV's broadcasting and streaming operations in a deal worth £1.6bn, subject to scrutiny and expected to complete in late 2027. Meanwhile, BBC Wales has announced 58 job cuts as part of efforts to save £500m.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Nvidia CEO's tenure under threat over affair with suspected Chinese spy
cards.content: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's 33-year tenure is under threat due to an extramarital affair with a customer being investigated for potential espionage. Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, who is suspected of feeding intelligence to China and smuggling AI chips into the country, has raised concerns over his future as CEO. The investigation, which is still ongoing, has sparked uncertainty about Nvidia's future, with the company's stock falling 6% Monday. Huang's leadership style, which has been described as demanding and intense, has been a key factor in Nvidia's success, but some experts believe that the company's bench is deep enough to continue without him. While Huang's potential departure would create uncertainty, it is unlikely to entirely upend the company's business, as major firms buying Nvidia's chips and software are unlikely to slash their capital spending.

cards.title: Pound Reaches 2016 High as Brexit Uncertainty Eases, Interest Rates Expected
cards.content: The pound has reached its highest level since the Brexit referendum in 2016, according to Bank of England figures. Sterling has risen significantly against the euro and dollar in recent weeks, ahead of an expected rise in interest rates. The pound's value rose to 86.4 on an index, where 100 equals the value in 2005. The Bank will officially confirm the calculation on Thursday. Some traders believe the UK's relative political stability, solid growth, and rapprochement with the European Union have contributed to the pound's rise. A stronger pound can help rein in inflation and increase buying power for consumers on imports and holidays.

cards.title: Nscale to Build UK's Largest AI Data Centre in Loughton, Despite Microsoft Pullout
cards.content: Nscale, a tech company, has reaffirmed its plans to build the UK's largest AI data centre in Loughton, Essex, despite Microsoft's decision to pull out of the project. Microsoft had agreed to fund a supercomputer at the site, but its involvement has been terminated. Nscale is exploring alternative power sources and maintaining a strong relationship with Microsoft for other projects globally. The data centre was expected to receive its power supply by the end of this year, but this has been delayed until the 2030s due to a London-wide grid issue. The project is expected to create 250 permanent jobs when it opens.
